title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams
title_zh: EvoTeam：通过团队演化实现多智能体协作

paragraphs.en: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on collaboration among specialized agents to solve complex tasks. Existing methods improve MAS by refining the prompts, skills, and execution strategies of individual agents based on task feedback. However, improving individual agents does not necessarily lead to better team collaboration. Recent studies have therefore extended evolution to the collaboration level, using collective execution experience to adjust team organization, and inter-agent interactions. Nevertheless, evolving collaboration across heterogeneous tasks remains challenging, as existing approaches often constrain team reorganization within a shared structure and reuse interaction rules across incompatible team contexts. In this paper, we propose EvoTeam , a collaboration-centric evolution framework that jointly evolves team organization, interaction rules, and individual agent skills through execution experience. It maintains a library of reusable teams, selecting or creating agent teams and guiding collaboration through team-specific interaction rules. Collaboration experience accumulates within compatible team contexts, while individual skills remain reusable across teams. Experiments across four benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness. Our code is available at https://github.com/DEEP-JLU/EvoTeam .
paragraphs.zh: 基于大语言模型的多智能体系统（MAS）依靠多个专业化智能体之间的协作来解决复杂任务。 现有方法通过基于任务反馈改进单个智能体的提示词、技能和执行策略来提升多智能体系统的性能。 然而，改进单个智能体并不一定会带来更好的团队协作。 因此，近期研究将演化扩展到协作层面，利用集体执行经验来调整团队组织以及智能体间的交互。 尽管如此，在异构任务上演化协作仍然具有挑战性，因为现有方法往往将团队重组限制在共享结构内，并在不兼容的团队上下文中复用交互规则。 在本文中，我们提出 EvoTeam，一个以协作为中心的演化框架，它通过执行经验联合演化团队组织、交互规则和单个智能体的技能。 它维护一个可复用团队的库，通过团队特定的交互规则来选择或创建智能体团队并引导协作。 协作经验在兼容的团队上下文中累积，而单个技能则可以跨团队复用。 在四个基准上的实验证明了其有效性。 我们的代码发布于 https://github.com/DEEP-JLU/EvoTeam 。

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) organize specialized agents into collaborative teams to effectively combine their complementary capabilities and accomplish complex tasks that require diverse expertise, sustained reasoning, and extensive tool interactions ( Guo et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2023 ; Hong et al., 2024 ) . Such collaboration has enabled applications ranging from information retrieval and software engineering to multi-step decision-making ( Wu et al., 2023 ; Qian et al., 2024 ; Ruan et al., 2026 ) . As these applications expand, enabling MAS to continuously improve through accumulated execution experience has become an important research direction ( Hao et al., 2026b ; Lin et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的多智能体系统（MAS）将专业化的智能体组织成协作团队，以有效结合它们的互补能力，完成需要多样专业知识、持续推理和大量工具交互的复杂任务（Guo et al., 2024；Chen et al., 2023；Hong et al., 2024）。 这种协作已催生了从信息检索、软件工程到多步决策等多种应用（Wu et al., 2023；Qian et al., 2024；Ruan et al., 2026）。 随着这些应用的扩展，使多智能体系统能够通过积累的执行经验持续改进，已成为一个重要的研究方向（Hao et al., 2026b；Lin et al., 2026）。

paragraphs.en: To enable such continual improvement, existing research has explored experience-driven evolution in multi-agent systems. A prominent direction focuses on improving the capabilities of individual agents through accumulated execution experience. By learning from previous task trajectories and feedback, agents can refine their prompts, acquire reusable skills, and improve their reasoning and tool-use strategies ( Hao et al., 2026b ; Zheng et al., 2025 ) . These improvements can be retained across tasks, allowing individual agents to progressively strengthen their task-solving capabilities ( Li et al., 2025 ) . Such experience-driven approaches provide an important foundation for MAS evolution by enabling agents to learn from previous executions rather than repeatedly solving tasks from scratch.
paragraphs.zh: 为了实现这种持续改进，现有研究已探索了多智能体系统中经验驱动的演化。 一个重要的方向是通过积累的执行经验来提升单个智能体的能力。 通过从先前的任务轨迹和反馈中学习，智能体可以改进其提示、获取可复用的技能，并提升其推理与工具使用策略 ( Hao et al., 2026b ; Zheng et al., 2025 ) 。 这些改进可以跨任务保留，使单个智能体能够逐步强化其解决问题的能力 ( Li et al., 2025 ) 。 这类经验驱动的方法通过使智能体能够从先前的执行中学习，而不是每次从零开始解决任务，为多智能体系统的演化提供了重要基础。

paragraphs.en: However, evolving better individual agents does not necessarily produce better collaborative teams. Multi-agent collaboration depends on how complementary capabilities are organized and coordinated toward a shared objective ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) . Even when agents possess necessary expertise, inappropriate responsibility assignments may prevent their capabilities from being effectively utilized, while incomplete information handoffs or insufficient verification may undermine correct individual contributions ( Cemri et al., 2025 ) . Effective MAS evolution must extend beyond improving what individual agents can do to improving how they organize, communicate, and collaborate.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，进化出更好的个体智能体并不一定会产生更好的协作团队。 多智能体协作取决于如何将互补能力组织起来并围绕共同目标进行协调（Zhuge et al., 2024；Zhou et al., 2026）。 即使智能体具备必要的专业知识，不恰当的职责分配也可能使其能力无法被有效利用，而信息传递不完整或验证不充分则可能破坏个体原本正确的贡献（Cemri et al., 2025）。 有效的多智能体系统（MAS）进化必须超越提升个体智能体的能力范畴，进而改进它们的组织、沟通与协作方式。

paragraphs.en: Recent studies have begun to extend experience-driven evolution from individual agents to multi-agent collaboration. Rather than refining agent capabilities in isolation, these approaches leverage collective execution experience to adapt team organization, adjust agent responsibilities, and improve inter-agent interactions ( Hao et al., 2026c ; Pan et al., 2026 ; Fei et al., 2026 ) . However, different tasks may require distinct combinations of agents, divisions of responsibility, and interaction rule ( Yue et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ; Kim et al., 2026 ) . Collaboration patterns learned from previous executions may not remain appropriate as task requirements change. This raises a critical question: how can MAS continuously evolve collaboration while adapting to heterogeneous tasks and preserving useful experience?
paragraphs.zh: 近期研究已开始将经验驱动的进化从单个智能体扩展到多智能体协作。 这些方法并非孤立地改进智能体能力，而是利用集体执行经验来调整团队组织、变更智能体职责并改进智能体间的交互 ( Hao et al., 2026c ; Pan et al., 2026 ; Fei et al., 2026 ) 。 然而，不同的任务可能需要不同的智能体组合、职责划分和交互规则 ( Yue et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ; Kim et al., 2026 ) 。 随着任务需求的变化，从以往执行中学到的协作模式可能不再适用。 这就引出了一个关键问题：多智能体系统如何在适应异构任务的同时持续进化协作，并保留有用的经验？

paragraphs.en: Despite recent advances, existing approaches face two critical limitations in collaboration evolution. (i) Constrained team reorganization. Existing approaches often adjust agent membership and responsibilities within a shared team, limiting their ability to maintain distinct collaboration patterns for tasks with different requirements. (ii) Inappropriate reuse of collaboration experience. Interaction rules learned from previous tasks are often tied to specific agent responsibilities and information dependencies. Reusing or updating these rules across incompatible collaboration contexts may introduce unsuitable handoffs or stopping conditions. Our preliminary study in Fig 2 further illustrates these difficulties: continued evolution across heterogeneous tasks can reduce task performance relative to target-only evolution, while representative execution trajectories reveal mismatches in team organization and interaction rule applicability.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管已有近期进展，现有方法在协作演化方面仍面临两个关键局限。 （i）受限的团队重组。 现有方法通常在共享团队内部调整智能体的成员构成与职责，这限制了它们针对具有不同需求的任务维持不同协作模式的能力。 （ii）对协作经验的不当复用。 从先前任务中学到的交互规则往往绑定于特定的智能体职责和信息依赖关系。 在不兼容的协作情境之间复用或更新这些规则，可能引入不合适的交接或停止条件。 我们在图2中的初步研究进一步说明了这些困难：在异构任务上持续演化会降低任务性能（相对于仅针对目标任务演化的结果），且代表性的执行轨迹揭示出团队组织与交互规则适用性方面的不匹配。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we propose EvoTeam , a collaboration-centric evolution framework that jointly evolves team organization, interaction rules, and individual agent skills through execution experience. EvoTeam organizes collaboration experience around task-appropriate teams, allowing compatible tasks to reuse and refine interaction rules while preserving individual agent skills across teams. Specifically, EvoTeam consists of three key stages. (i) Adaptive Agent Team Composition maintains a library of agent teams, selecting a compatible team or creating a new one according to task requirements. (ii) Team-Scoped Collaboration coordinates task execution through task-specific responsibility assignments and applicable team-specific interaction rules, allowing tasks with compatible collaboration requirements to reuse accumulated coordination experience while keeping rule updates independent across teams. (iii) Multi-Level Experience Evolution leverages execution traces and task feedback to refine team organization, update team-specific interaction rules, and improve individual agent skills. While collaboration experience evolves within corresponding teams, individual skills remain reusable across team contexts. Our contributions are summarized as follows:

paragraphs.en: In this section, we investigate whether experience accumulated on previous tasks benefits continued evolution of MAS across heterogeneous tasks. We compare performance across evolution settings and examine how team organization and interaction-rule applicability may limit experience reuse.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们研究在先前任务上积累的经验是否有助于多智能体系统（MAS）在异构任务间的持续演化。 我们比较了不同演化设置下的性能，并考察团队组织和交互规则适用性可能如何限制经验的复用。

paragraphs.en: In our preliminary experiments, Meta-Team exhibits lower target-task performance after cross-task evolution than after target-only evolution. To examine this degradation, we evaluate two cross-task (CT) evolution settings. In both settings, the system inherits an evolved MAS and continues its evolution on the target training tasks. We use target-only Meta-Team as the primary reference and Vanilla MAS as a non-evolutionary reference. Inter-CT starts from another benchmark with an unsuitable team template, whereas Intra-CT starts from another task category within the same benchmark with a compatible team template. As shown in Figure 2(a) , both settings underperform target-only Meta-Team on all three metrics. These results suggest that prior experience does not necessarily benefit continued evolution, even when a compatible team template is retained.
paragraphs.zh: 在初步实验中，Meta-Team 在跨任务演化后的目标任务性能低于仅目标演化后的性能。 为探究这一性能下降，我们评估了两种跨任务（CT）演化设置。 在这两种设置中，系统继承一个已演化的多智能体系统（MAS），并在目标任务训练集上继续演化。 我们使用仅目标演化的 Meta-Team 作为主要参照，使用原始 MAS 作为非演化参照。 Inter-CT 从另一个基准出发，其团队模板不适用；而 Intra-CT 从同一基准内的另一任务类别出发，其团队模板兼容。 如图 2(a) 所示，两种设置在全部三项指标上均不及仅目标演化的 Meta-Team。 这些结果表明，先前的经验并不一定有利于持续演化，即使保留了兼容的团队模板。

paragraphs.en: Our preliminary study suggests that retaining prior experience alone is insufficient for effective MAS evolution across heterogeneous tasks. Although accumulated agent skills may remain useful across team contexts, reusing the original team template and interaction rules without accounting for new task requirements can constrain subsequent evolution. (i) Team adaptation should maintain distinct collaboration structures. Selecting or creating task-appropriate teams enables reorganization to meet changing collaboration requirements. (ii) Interaction rules should be shared and refined only among tasks with compatible collaboration requirements. A clear reuse scope helps prevent rule updates for one task type from disrupting the coordination required by others. Guided by these principles, we develop EvoTeam to support the accumulation and selective reuse of collaboration experience across heterogeneous tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的初步研究表明，仅保留先前经验不足以实现跨异构任务的有效多智能体系统演进。 尽管积累的智能体技能在团队情境之间可能仍然有用，但在不考虑新任务需求的情况下复用原始团队模板和交互规则，可能会限制后续的演进。 (i) 团队适应应保持不同的协作结构。 选择或创建适合任务的团队，能够通过重组来满足不断变化的协作需求。 (ii) 交互规则应仅在协作需求兼容的任务之间共享和优化。 明确的复用范围有助于防止某一任务类型的规则更新破坏其他任务所需的协调。 在这些原则的指导下，我们开发了 EvoTeam，以支持跨异构任务的协作经验积累与选择性复用。

paragraphs.en: Our preliminary study indicates that experience reuse across heterogeneous tasks requires flexible team formation and selective reuse of interaction rules. Motivated by these requirements, we develop EvoTeam , a framework that selects or creates task-appropriate agent teams to reorganize agents and evolves interaction rules within each team. Figure 3 summarizes its three stages per task. (i) Adaptive Agent Team Composition: EvoTeam selects or creates a task-appropriate agent team and recruits agents from its candidate roster. (ii) Team-Scoped Collaboration: Agents use accumulated skills to complete subtasks and consult the selected agent team’s interaction rules. (iii) Multi-Level Experience Evolution: Execution evidence refines agent teams, updates team-specific interaction rules, and evolves agent skills for reuse across agent teams.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的初步研究表明，跨异构任务的经验复用需要灵活的团队组建以及对交互规则的选择性复用。 受这些需求的启发，我们提出了 EvoTeam，该框架通过选择或创建适合任务的智能体团队来重新组织智能体，并在每个团队内部演化交互规则。 图 3 总结了其在每个任务上的三个阶段。 （i）自适应智能体团队组建：EvoTeam 选择或创建适合任务的智能体团队，并从其候选名册中招募智能体。 （ii）团队范围内的协作：智能体利用积累的技能完成子任务，并参考所选智能体团队的交互规则。 （iii）多层次经验演化：执行证据用于优化智能体团队、更新团队专属的交互规则，并演化智能体技能以供跨智能体团队复用。

paragraphs.en: Individual-benchmark evolution optimizes AgentSquare, the experience-driven baselines, and EvoTeam on each benchmark/subset’s evolution split; SA, MAS, and OWL run without prior evolution. paragraphs.en: Obs. 1. EvoTeam achieves strong performance across benchmarks with different task requirements. Under individual-benchmark evolution, EvoTeam achieves the highest average score of 58.85 and leads on four of the six evaluation metrics. Its advantage over Meta-Team, the strongest competing method by average score, spans GAIA, both LoCoBench tasks, and BeyondSWE DepMig. The margin reaches five points (78.00 versus 73.00) on GAIA. EvoTeam also outperforms the MAS baseline on every metric. The breadth of these gains shows that the framework is effective across different collaboration requirements, highlighting the value of task-conditioned team and the interaction experience retained within them.
paragraphs.zh: 观察 1。 EvoTeam 在具有不同任务要求的多个基准测试上均取得了强劲的表现。 在单基准进化设置下，EvoTeam 取得了 58.85 的最高平均分，并在六项评估指标中的四项上处于领先。 相对于按平均分衡量最强的竞争方法 Meta-Team，其优势覆盖 GAIA、两个 LoCoBench 任务以及 BeyondSWE DepMig。 在 GAIA 上，这一差距达到五分（78.00 对 73.00）。 EvoTeam 在每一项指标上也优于 MAS 基线。 这些提升的广度表明该框架在不同的协作要求下均有效，凸显了任务条件化团队以及团队内保留的交互经验的价值。

paragraphs.en: Obs. 2. EvoTeam sustains its advantage when evolution combines heterogeneous benchmarks. Under the mixed-benchmark, EvoTeam ranks first on all six metrics and achieves an average score of 59.58, surpassing Meta-Team by 4.03 points. Its lead is clear on GAIA and LOCA, while extending across the evaluation suite. EvoTeam ’s average score improves under the mixed-benchmark evolution relative to its individual-benchmark result. Meta-Team’s average score declines under the same comparison. These results demonstrate EvoTeam ’s advantage in reusing collaboration experience across the heterogeneous tasks with the different coordination requirements.

paragraphs.en: To address Q2, we examine whether EvoTeam ’s evolved team and interaction rules can be reused across LLM backbones. We use DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GPT-5.6-Luna as the evolution and evaluation LLMs, and evaluate GAIA and the two LoCoBench tasks. For each configuration, we compare EvoTeam with the unevolved MAS baseline using the same evaluation LLM. Table 2 reports the same- and cross-backbone evaluation results. We summarize two observations below.

paragraphs.en: Obs. 3. Evolved collaboration transfers across backbones in both directions. When evolution and evaluation use different LLMs, EvoTeam consistently outperforms MAS in all six configurations. On GAIA, both backbones benefit from artifacts evolved by the other model. The gains reach 5.00 and 18.00 points for GPT-5.6-Luna and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash respectively. Both LoCoBench tasks also improve in each transfer direction, showing that the effect extends across task settings. These bidirectional gains demonstrate that the collaboration experience accumulated through EvoTeam ’s team-indexed evolution transfers effectively between the two evaluated LLM backbones.
paragraphs.zh: 观察3。 演化出的协作在两个主干之间双向迁移。 当演化与评估使用不同的LLM时，EvoTeam在全部六种配置中始终优于MAS。 在GAIA上，两个主干均从由另一模型演化得到的工件中受益。 GPT-5.6-Luna和DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash的增益分别达到5.00分和18.00分。 两个LoCoBench任务在每个迁移方向上也都有提升，表明该效应可扩展到不同任务设置。 这些双向增益表明，通过EvoTeam按团队索引的演化所积累的协作经验，能够在两个受评估的LLM主干之间有效迁移。

paragraphs.en: Obs. 4. Cross-backbone transfer retains performance close to the same-backbone setting. The two LoCoBench tasks also show similarly small performance gaps for both evaluation backbones. This observed stability highlights EvoTeam ’s robustness to changes in the evolution LLM and shows that its team-indexed collaboration experience remains effective across different backbone configurations.

paragraphs.en: Obs. 5. Learned interaction rules strengthen collaboration within team. Across all four tasks, the full EvoTeam outperforms the variant that retains templates but removes interaction rules. The largest gains appear on GAIA and LOCA, where the rules add 10.00 and 8.75 points. The resulting performance gap supports the importance of retaining experience about how agents work together across successive task executions, beyond determining which agents participate. The smaller gains on the coding tasks indicate that the contribution of this guidance varies across tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 观察 5。 学习到的交互规则能加强团队内部的协作。 在全部四项任务中，完整的 EvoTeam 都优于保留模板但移除交互规则的变体。 最大的提升出现在 GAIA 和 LOCA 上，交互规则分别带来 10.00 和 8.75 分的提升。 由此产生的性能差距表明，除了决定哪些智能体参与之外，保留关于智能体如何在连续任务执行中协同工作的经验也十分重要。 在编码任务上较小的提升表明，这类指导的贡献因任务而异。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we presented EvoTeam , a framework for continual collaboration evolution across heterogeneous tasks. It maintains a library of reusable teams and jointly evolves their organization, team-specific interaction rules, and individual agent skills, accumulating coordination experience within compatible team contexts while preserving skill reuse across teams. Across four benchmarks and six task categories, EvoTeam leads all six metrics under mixed-benchmark evolution, averaging 59.58 versus 55.55 for the strongest baseline. Cross-backbone evaluations and ablations further support the transferability of evolved collaboration experience and the value of jointly evolving team organization and coordination practices.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们提出了 EvoTeam，一个面向异构任务持续协作演化的框架。 它维护一个可复用团队库，并联合演化团队的组织方式、团队专属交互规则以及个体智能体技能，在兼容的团队上下文中积累协作经验，同时保留技能的跨团队复用。 在四个基准和六个任务类别上，EvoTeam 在混合基准演化下于全部六项指标中领先，平均得分为 59.58，而最强基线为 55.55。 跨骨干模型的评估与消融实验进一步支持了演化后的协作经验的可迁移性，以及联合演化团队组织与协作实践的价值。

paragraphs.en: Our evaluation does not systematically examine collaborative evolution in multimodal interactive environments. In such settings, agents need to interpret visual observations, communicate relevant evidence, and coordinate actions as the environment changes. Further investigation is needed into how multimodal execution traces can guide the refinement of team organization, interaction rules, and agent skills. Future work could extend EvoTeam to these settings and evaluate how accumulated collaboration experience supports tasks involving visual perception and interaction. Additionally, EvoTeam accumulates experience through explicit updates while keeping the LLM parameters fixed. The effective use of this experience depends on the base model’s ability to correctly interpret and apply the stored guidance. Combining experience reuse with model adaptation could help internalize frequently useful coordination practices.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的评估并未系统地考察多模态交互环境中的协作演化。 在这类环境中，智能体需要理解视觉观察结果、交流相关证据，并随着环境变化协调行动。 关于多模态执行轨迹如何指导团队组织、交互规则和智能体技能的改进，仍需进一步研究。 未来的工作可以将 EvoTeam 扩展到这些环境中，并评估积累的协作经验如何支持涉及视觉感知与交互的任务。 此外，EvoTeam 通过显式更新来积累经验，同时保持大语言模型（LLM）参数不变。 这些经验的有效利用取决于基础模型能否正确理解并应用所存储的指导信息。 将经验复用与模型适配相结合，有助于将频繁有用的协作实践内化。

paragraphs.en: EvoTeam aims to improve multi-agent collaboration through reusable teams and accumulated execution experience. Like other LLM-based agent systems, it may inherit biases from underlying models and produce inaccurate outputs or unintended tool actions. Persistent experience accumulation also requires attention to sensitive information retained in execution traces and reusable knowledge. Applications beyond the evaluated benchmarks should therefore incorporate appropriate access controls, privacy protection, and human oversight for consequential actions. Accumulated interaction rules and agent skills should be reviewed for their suitability before reuse in new contexts. The use of underlying models, datasets, and tools should respect their respective licenses and usage policies.
paragraphs.zh: EvoTeam 旨在通过可复用的团队和积累的执行经验来改进多智能体协作。 与其他基于 LLM 的智能体系统一样，它可能继承底层模型的偏见，并产生不准确的输出或非预期的工具操作。 持续的经验积累还需要注意执行轨迹和可复用知识中保留的敏感信息。 因此，在所评估基准之外的应用中，应针对关键性操作采取适当的访问控制、隐私保护和人工监督。 积累的交互规则和智能体技能在复用到新场景之前，应先审查其适用性。 底层模型、数据集和工具的使用应遵守其各自的许可证和使用政策。

paragraphs.en: (i) GAIA. ( Mialon et al., 2024 ) evaluates general-purpose assistants on real-world questions requiring reasoning, web browsing, tool use, and, for some questions, multimodal understanding. Questions are organized into three difficulty levels and have unambiguous reference answers; some include supplementary files. Following Meta-Team, we use the 120-instance validation subset, with 20 instances for evolution and 100 disjoint instances for holdout evaluation. The evolution split contains 6, 9, and 5 instances from Levels 1, 2, and 3, respectively; the holdout split contains 38, 49, and 13 instances. Agents can read and write files, run shell commands, search online, and fetch webpages.

paragraphs.en: (ii) LoCoBench. paragraphs.en: (iii) LOCA-Bench. ( Zeng et al., 2026 ) evaluates language agents under controllable context growth by scaling environment states while preserving task semantics. The full benchmark contains 15 task types, seven environment-description lengths (8K, 16K, 32K, 64K, 96K, 128K, and 256K), and five environment seeds. Environment-description length measures the tokenized information available through the task environment’s tool outputs; it is distinct from the model’s context-window limit. We select eight task types spanning e-commerce, academic, and education workflows, summarized in Table 3 . Evolution uses these eight tasks at 96K with seeds 101 and 102, giving 8 × 2 = 16 8\times 2=16 cases. Holdout evaluation uses seeds { 42,123,456,789 , 2024 } \{42,123,456,789,2024\} at 8K, 16K, 32K, 64K, 128K, and 256K, giving 8 × 5 × 6 = 240 8\times 5\times 6=240 cases. The evolution and holdout configurations are disjoint in both environment seeds and description lengths, testing cross-seed and cross-scale generalization for the selected task types. Each case runs with isolated local mock MCP services and is scored by the corresponding native environment-state evaluator.

paragraphs.en: (iv) BeyondSWE. ( Chen et al., 2026 ) evaluates software engineering beyond single-repository bug fixing. Its 500 instances are drawn from 246 real-world GitHub repositories and cover cross-repository issue resolution, domain-specific fixes, dependency migration, and repository generation from specifications. We use the CrossRepo and DepMigrate tracks. CrossRepo requires reasoning with information from related external repositories, while DepMigrate requires repository-wide changes to accommodate breaking dependency updates. Following Meta-Team, we randomly select 20 instances per track for evolution and hold out the rest: CrossRepo has 200 instances (20 evolution, 180 holdout) and DepMigrate has 178 (20 evolution, 158 holdout). Each track is evolved separately and evaluated on its own holdout split. Each instance runs in an isolated repository environment, and submitted changes are evaluated with native Fail-to-Pass (F2P) and Pass-to-Pass (P2P) tests.
paragraphs.zh: (iv) BeyondSWE。 （Chen et al., 2026）评估了超越单仓库缺陷修复的软件工程任务。 其 500 个实例来自 246 个真实的 GitHub 仓库，涵盖跨仓库问题解决、领域特定修复、依赖迁移以及根据规格说明生成仓库。 我们使用 CrossRepo 和 DepMigrate 两个赛道。 CrossRepo 需要利用相关外部仓库中的信息进行推理，而 DepMigrate 需要对整个仓库进行修改以适配破坏性的依赖更新。 参照 Meta-Team 的做法，我们在每个赛道中随机选取 20 个实例用于进化，其余作为留存集：CrossRepo 有 200 个实例（20 个用于进化，180 个留存），DepMigrate 有 178 个（20 个用于进化，158 个留存）。 每个赛道分别独立进化，并在各自的留存集上评估。 每个实例都在隔离的仓库环境中运行，提交的变更通过原生的 Fail-to-Pass（F2P）和 Pass-to-Pass（P2P）测试进行评估。

paragraphs.en: (v) Mixed-Benchmark. combines the four source benchmarks into a single mixed-task setting. Its evolution split contains 116 instances: 20 GAIA, 20 LoCoBench FI, 20 LoCoBench CR, 16 LOCA-Bench, 20 BeyondSWE CrossRepo, and 20 BeyondSWE DepMigrate. These instances are materialized once in a fixed global-shuffle order using seed 20260828. A shared system evolves sequentially over the mixed task stream and is frozen before evaluating the holdout groups. Each task retains its source benchmark’s tools, environment, output contract, and evaluator. Results are reported using the respective source-native evaluation metrics for each of the corresponding holdout groups.

paragraphs.en: (i) GAIA. We report answer accuracy using the official evaluator ( Mialon et al., 2024 ) . A prediction is correct only if the complete final answer matches the reference under the evaluator’s normalization rules. These rules handle differences in capitalization, whitespace, punctuation, and numeric formatting as appropriate to the answer type. For list-valued answers, the number of elements and all corresponding elements must match. Both semantically similar but unmatched answers and partially correct answers are scored as incorrect.
paragraphs.zh: (i) GAIA。 我们使用官方评估器（Mialon et al., 2024）报告答案准确率。 只有当完整最终答案在评估器的规范化规则下与参考答案匹配时，该预测才算正确。 这些规则根据答案类型酌情处理大小写、空白、标点符号和数字格式的差异。 对于列表型答案，元素数量以及所有对应的元素都必须匹配。 语义相似但不匹配的答案以及部分正确的答案均计为错误。

paragraphs.en: (ii) LOCA-Bench. We report task success rate under the official execution-based evaluation protocol ( Zeng et al., 2026 ) . Task-specific evaluation scripts check whether the final environment state satisfies the required outcomes, such as correctly updated records or generated artifacts. Each run receives a binary score: one if the task passes the evaluator and zero otherwise. Success therefore depends on the resulting environment state, rather than the agent’s mere textual claim of completion.
paragraphs.zh: (ii) LOCA-Bench。 我们在官方基于执行的评估协议（Zeng et al., 2026）下报告任务成功率。 特定于任务的评估脚本检查最终环境状态是否满足所需的结果，例如正确更新的记录或生成的产物。 每次运行获得一个二元评分：若任务通过评估器则为一，否则为零。 因此，成功取决于所产生的环境状态，而非智能体仅凭文本声称完成。

paragraphs.en: (iii) BeyondSWE. For CrossRepo and DepMigrate, we report the percentage of resolved instances ( Chen et al., 2026 ) . paragraphs.en: We compare our method with the following seven baselines. All these methods use GPT-5.6-Luna for task execution and, where applicable, for reflection and optimization. They share the same benchmark-specific tool access, resource budgets, and evolution/holdout splits as EvoTeam .
paragraphs.zh: 我们将我们的方法与以下七个基线方法进行比较。 所有这些方法都使用 GPT-5.6-Luna 来执行任务，并在适用的情况下用于反思和优化。 它们与 EvoTeam 共享相同的基准特定工具访问权限、资源预算以及进化/留出集划分。

sents.en: We compare our method with the following seven baselines.
sents.zh: 我们将我们的方法与以下七个基线方法进行比较。

sents.en: All these methods use GPT-5.6-Luna for task execution and, where applicable, for reflection and optimization.
sents.zh: 所有这些方法都使用 GPT-5.6-Luna 来执行任务，并在适用的情况下用于反思和优化。

sents.en: They share the same benchmark-specific tool access, resource budgets, and evolution/holdout splits as EvoTeam .
sents.zh: 它们与 EvoTeam 共享相同的基准特定工具访问权限、资源预算以及进化/留出集划分。

paragraphs.en: (i) SA uses a single agent with a ReAct-style workflow ( Yao et al., 2023 ) , alternating between reasoning and tool use to solve each given task, without involving any form of experience-driven evolution.
paragraphs.zh: (i) SA 使用单个智能体，采用 ReAct 风格的工作流（Yao et al., 2023），在推理与工具使用之间交替进行以解决每个给定任务，不涉及任何形式的经验驱动演化。

paragraphs.en: (ii) MAS uses a multi-agent team with the same collaboration structure as ours. The team configuration remains unchanged across tasks, with no experience-driven evolution. MAS is evaluated directly and independently on the holdout split.
paragraphs.zh: (ii) MAS 使用与我们相同的协作结构的智能体团队。 该团队配置在各个任务中保持不变，没有基于经验的演化。 MAS 直接且独立地在留出集上进行评估。

sents.en: (ii) MAS uses a multi-agent team with the same collaboration structure as ours.
sents.zh: (ii) MAS 使用与我们相同的协作结构的智能体团队。

sents.en: The team configuration remains unchanged across tasks, with no experience-driven evolution.
sents.zh: 该团队配置在各个任务中保持不变，没有基于经验的演化。

sents.en: MAS is evaluated directly and independently on the holdout split.
sents.zh: MAS 直接且独立地在留出集上进行评估。

paragraphs.en: (iii) OWL ( Hu et al., 2025a ) organizes task execution through a Planner–Coordinator–Worker hierarchy. We use the official implementation with its original structure under the common backbone, tool-access, and budget settings. OWL does not perform experience-driven evolution and is evaluated directly on the corresponding holdout split.
paragraphs.zh: (iii) OWL（Hu et al., 2025a）通过规划器–协调器–执行者的层级结构组织任务执行。 我们使用官方实现并保留其原有结构，在共同的骨干模型、工具访问和预算设置下进行评估。 OWL 不进行经验驱动的演化，而是直接在相应的留出集上进行评估。

sents.en: (iii) OWL ( Hu et al., 2025a ) organizes task execution through a Planner–Coordinator–Worker hierarchy.
sents.zh: (iii) OWL（Hu et al., 2025a）通过规划器–协调器–执行者的层级结构组织任务执行。

sents.en: We use the official implementation with its original structure under the common backbone, tool-access, and budget settings.
sents.zh: 我们使用官方实现并保留其原有结构，在共同的骨干模型、工具访问和预算设置下进行评估。

sents.en: OWL does not perform experience-driven evolution and is evaluated directly on the corresponding holdout split.
sents.zh: OWL 不进行经验驱动的演化，而是直接在相应的留出集上进行评估。

paragraphs.en: (iv) AgentSquare ( Shang et al., 2025 ) searches a modular agent design space comprising planning, reasoning, tool use, and memory. We use its official implementation and released search configuration, with the candidate scaffold pool adopted from Meta-Team. Search is conducted on the designated evolution split, and the selected configuration is kept fixed for the subsequent holdout evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: (iv) AgentSquare（Shang et al., 2025）在由规划、推理、工具使用和记忆组成的模块化智能体设计空间中进行搜索。 我们使用其官方实现和公开发布的搜索配置，候选脚手架池采用自 Meta-Team。 搜索在指定的演化划分上进行，所选配置在后续保留集评估中保持固定。

sents.en: Search is conducted on the designated evolution split, and the selected configuration is kept fixed for the subsequent holdout evaluation.
sents.zh: 搜索在指定的演化划分上进行，所选配置在后续保留集评估中保持固定。

paragraphs.en: (v) Skill-MAS ( Lin et al., 2026 ) evolves a meta-skill that guides task decomposition, agent construction, and workflow orchestration. It combines multiple trajectory rollouts with selective reflection to distill reusable orchestration principles from execution experience. We use the official implementation with k = 2 k=2 , sampling two separate trajectories per task in each evolution round. Evolution uses only the designated evolution split, and the evolved meta-skill is frozen before holdout evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: (v) Skill-MAS（Lin et al., 2026）演化出一个元技能，用于指导任务分解、智能体构建和工作流编排。 它将多次轨迹采样与选择性反思相结合，从执行经验中提炼出可复用的编排原则。 我们使用官方实现，取 k=2，在每一轮演化中为每个任务采样两条独立轨迹。 演化仅使用指定的演化划分，且演化后的元技能在留出集评估之前被冻结。

sents.en: (v) Skill-MAS ( Lin et al., 2026 ) evolves a meta-skill that guides task decomposition, agent construction, and workflow orchestration.

paragraphs.en: (vi) ReCreate ( Hao et al., 2026b ) is an experience-driven framework for optimizing agent scaffolds. Its agent-as-optimizer mechanism inspects execution trajectories, submitted artifacts, and evaluation feedback to propose changes to prompts, tools, and memory. Instance-level proposals are synthesized into reusable updates to the shared scaffold. We use the official implementation under the common model, tool-access, and budget settings. Evolution uses only the designated evolution split, and the final scaffold is frozen for holdout evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: (vi) ReCreate（Hao et al., 2026b）是一个用于优化智能体脚手架的体验驱动框架。 其“智能体即优化器”机制会检查执行轨迹、提交的产物和评估反馈，以提出对提示词、工具和记忆的修改建议。 实例级别的建议会被整合为对共享脚手架的可复用更新。 我们使用官方实现，并在通用的模型、工具访问和预算设置下运行。 进化仅使用指定的进化数据划分，最终脚手架被冻结用于保留集评估。

paragraphs.en: (vii) Meta-Team ( Hao et al., 2026c ) improves multi-agent systems through collaborative analysis of execution experience. We use its official implementation and apply its experience-driven evolution procedure specifically on the predefined designated evolution split.
paragraphs.zh: (vii) Meta-Team（Hao et al., 2026c）通过对执行经验的协作分析来改进多智能体系统。 智能体保留各自的本地执行上下文，并交换相关发现，以支持对单个智能体行为、智能体间协作以及团队组织的更新。 我们使用其官方实现，并将其基于经验的演化流程专门应用于预定义的指定演化划分。

paragraphs.en: Each benchmark or track is treated as an independent evolution and evaluation setting. SA, MAS, and OWL are evaluated directly on the holdout split without prior evolution. paragraphs.en: ReCreate, Meta-Team, Skill-MAS, and EvoTeam participate in mixed-benchmark evolution. The evolution stream contains 116 instances: 20 GAIA, 20 LoCoBench FI, 20 LoCoBench CR, 16 LOCA-Bench, 20 BeyondSWE CrossRepo, and 20 BeyondSWE DepMigrate. These instances are shuffled once using seed 20260828, and the order is fixed across methods. All four methods start from the same shared initial agent pool. Each method evolves a single system over the mixed task stream using its own update procedure, carrying experience across benchmarks. Each task retains its source-specific tools, environment, output contract, and evaluator. The final system is frozen and evaluated separately on all source holdout groups using their native metrics.

paragraphs.en: The full framework also outperforms the variant without both reusable agent teams and interaction rules in all six settings. On GAIA, LOCA, LoCoBench Feat, and BeyondSWE CrossR, removing the two components lowers performance, supporting the value of combining team organization with learned coordination guidance. Despite these exceptions, the complete design provides the strongest overall results across the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs.en: Figure 7 shows that EvoTeam achieves the highest score at the lowest estimated cost on GAIA and both LoCoBench tasks. On BeyondSWE DepMig, it outperforms Meta-Team and ReCreate at a lower cost; AgentSquare and OWL are cheaper but score lower. This trade-off is consistent with the reuse mechanisms: reusable agent teams provide established divisions of work, while interaction rules supply relevant coordination guidance. Reusing both reduces the need to establish same collaboration procedures anew for tasks with compatible requirements.

paragraphs.en: We present seven core prompts covering team selection, cold-start team composition, task execution, and post-task reflection. The following subsections explain each prompt’s purpose and role in the overall process. The corresponding numbered prompts are collected afterward and specify the role, inputs, core rules, and output format. Repetitive instructions and tool-call schemas are omitted; benchmark-specific execution requirements and output formats are appended to each task. Related engineering guidance emphasizes explicit instructions, well-defined tool interfaces, and the selection of relevant context for reliable agent execution and coordination. ( Anthropic, 2024 ; Anthropic, 2025a ) .

paragraphs.en: Prompt 1 (Figure 10 ) determines whether an incoming task can reuse an existing agent team or requires a cold start. The decision is based on the task’s specific collaboration requirements, complementary agent roles, and verification needs, rather than topic similarity alone. This stage selects the collaboration structure while leaving individual agent recruitment to the Chairman. When no existing team is suitable, it produces a provisional team description for subsequent team composition; admission to the team library is decided after task execution.
paragraphs.zh: 提示词 1（图 10）判断传入的任务能否复用现有的智能体团队，还是需要冷启动。 该决策基于任务的具体协作需求、互补的智能体角色以及验证需求，而非仅凭主题相似性。 此阶段确定协作结构，而将各个智能体的招募留给 Chairman（主席）。 当没有合适的现有团队时，它会生成一份临时团队描述用于后续的团队组建；是否纳入团队库则在任务执行之后决定。

paragraphs.en: Prompt 7 (Figure 15 ) extracts reusable improvements to an individual agent’s execution behavior from its trace and evaluation feedback. Short behavioral instructions are stored as prompt patches, while repeatable procedures with explicit activation conditions and verification steps are stored as skills. The prompt favors small, supported updates that preserve existing valid behavior and avoid duplication. It excludes one-off task answers and does not attribute team-assignment, handoff, or infrastructure failures to the agent’s reusable capabilities.Reusable procedural knowledge is also central to Agent Skills, which packages instructions, scripts, and supporting resources for agents to discover and load when needed ( Anthropic, 2025b ) .

paragraphs.en: We present four cases drawn from the mixed-benchmark evolution and holdout splits. Cases 1 and 2 concern what is retained during evolution: Case 1 shows that a task-derived update stays confined to the selected team’s rule set instead of overwriting experience accumulated for other collaboration patterns, and Case 2 follows one team across an interleaved LoCoBench and BeyondSWE sequence. Cases 3 and 4 use the frozen library on the holdout split: Case 3 shows three tasks from three different benchmarks selecting the same team, and Case 4 compares EvoTeam with Meta-Team on a single task, tracing the score difference to specific team configuration and handoff requirements.
paragraphs.zh: 我们展示了四个案例，这些案例取自混合基准演化与留出集划分。 案例 1 和案例 2 关注演化过程中保留了什么：案例 1 表明，源于任务的更新仅停留在所选团队的规则集内，而不会覆盖为其他协作模式积累的经验；案例 2 则跟踪一个团队完成交错进行的 LoCoBench 与 BeyondSWE 序列。 案例 3 和案例 4 在留出集上使用冻结库：案例 3 显示来自三个不同基准的三个任务选择了同一个团队；案例 4 在单个任务上比较 EvoTeam 与 Meta-Team，将分数差异追溯到具体的团队配置与交接要求。

paragraphs.en: Before this task, the shared profiles of context analyst, implementer, and verifier contained 45, 43, and 31 notes, respectively. These covered numerical reasoning from GAIA, repository analysis and code verification from BeyondSWE, and record reconciliation and calendar operations from LOCA-Bench. The Chairman reported 62 successful sends, but evaluation returned 0.0 with “Email verification failed.” Reflection identified that address existence had been checked without validating sent-message bodies. It then replaced each accumulated notes list with a single note. Specialized analysis and verification requirements disappeared, while the implementer’s new advice restricted recruitment to tasks requiring artifact changes, despite earlier guidance covering calendar operations. These replacements were shared by teammate name without a benchmark or family condition. A bulk-side-effect verification rule was appended to the shared constitution, retaining its engineering clauses.
paragraphs.zh: 在此任务之前，上下文分析者、实现者和验证者的共享档案分别包含45、43和31条笔记。 这些笔记涵盖来自GAIA的数值推理、来自BeyondSWE的仓库分析与代码验证，以及来自LOCA-Bench的记录核对与日历操作。 主席报告成功发送了62封邮件，但评估返回0.0，并给出「邮件验证失败」的信息。反思发现，此前仅检查了地址是否存在，而未验证已发送邮件的内容。 随后，它把每个累积的笔记列表替换为单条笔记。 专门的分析与验证要求消失了，而实现者的新建议将招募范围限制在需要修改工件的任务上，尽管此前的指导涵盖了日历操作。 这些替换按队友名称在队友之间共享，没有任何基准或家族条件。 一条批量副作用验证规则被追加到共享章程中，同时保留了其工程条款。

paragraphs.en: Research on agent improvement explores how feedback can refine task-solving behavior and produce reusable knowledge. Early approaches establish feedback-based refinement through iterative output revision and reflection-guided repeated attempts, with different scopes of experience retention ( Madaan et al., 2023 ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) . Self-Refine improves generated outputs through self-generated feedback, while Reflexion retains verbal reflections in episodic memory to guide subsequent trials. ExpeL extends experience reuse across tasks by extracting natural-language insights from past executions and recalling these insights alongside the relevant previous experiences during subsequent task solving ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) .

paragraphs.en: Another line of work converts interaction experience into reusable procedural knowledge and revised execution scaffolds ( Wang et al., 2023 ; Zheng et al., 2025 ; Hao et al., 2026b ) . Voyager accumulates executable skills through open-ended environment interaction, while SkillWeaver enables web agents to discover and practice skills, distilling interaction experience into reusable APIs. ReCreate reasons over interaction histories to identify causes of success and failure, translating execution experience into scaffold revisions and reusable domain patterns. Mem 2 Evolve connects experience accumulation with capability expansion by using experience memory to guide the creation of reusable tools and expert agents ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) . Agentic Context Engineering (ACE) instead maintains evolving context playbooks through generation, reflection, and curation, using incremental updates to preserve useful knowledge across executions ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) . Within multi-agent collaboration, MAEL maintains individual experience pools and retrieves high-reward, task-relevant examples to improve agents’ subsequent reasoning steps ( Li et al., 2025 ) . Together, these studies improve agent designs and retain reflections, skills, and execution knowledge beyond a single response. However, analyses of multi-agent failures and scaling behavior show that collaborative performance also depends on inter-agent alignment and the compatibility between coordination structures and task requirements ( Cemri et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2026 ) . This leaves a distinct question for collaborative evolution: how should accumulated capabilities be organized and coordinated when tasks require different responsibilities and information handoffs?

paragraphs.en: At the collaboration level, improvement extends to interactions and the structures connecting agent behaviors. paragraphs.en: Automated optimization further treats agent prompts, graph connectivity, and executable workflows as searchable components ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025c ) . GPTSwarm optimizes node-level prompts and graph connectivity, MASS interleaves prompt and topology optimization, and AFlow searches over code-represented workflows using execution feedback.EvoMAC uses textual backpropagation from environmental feedback to revise multi-agent collaboration networks, while EvoFlow evolves a population of diverse workflows through retrieval, crossover, and mutation ( Hu et al., 2025c ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) . ScoreFlow extends workflow optimization through score-based preference learning, while EvoAgent uses evolutionary operators to generate diverse agents from an initial agent framework ( Wang et al., 2025a ; Yuan et al., 2025 ) . To accommodate varying task requirements, query-dependent approaches learn to select or generate collaboration architectures, agent roles, and model assignments according to the input query ( Zhang et al., 2025b ; Gao et al., 2025 ; Yue et al., 2025 ) . These methods make collaboration structures explicit optimization targets and support task-dependent system construction.

paragraphs.en: Experience-driven approaches investigate how execution knowledge can support subsequent collaboration, including retrieval-based agent memory, collective reflection, and reusable orchestration knowledge ( Yang et al., 2025 ; Hao et al., 2026c ; Lin et al., 2026 ) . AgentNet combines retrieval-based memory with decentralized coordination, adapting connectivity and task routing according to local expertise and context. DecentMem gives each agent separate memory pools for consolidated experience and generated exploratory candidates, adjusting their relative weights through online feedback ( Hao et al., 2026a ) . Meta-Team preserves individual execution contexts and enables post-task evidence exchange, supporting evolution of agent behaviors, inter-agent coordination, and team organization. Skill-based approaches connect reusable knowledge with changes to multi-agent collaboration: SkillMAS couples skill evolution with evidence-guided MAS restructuring, while Skill-MAS represents orchestration knowledge as an evolvable Meta-Skill refined through multi-trajectory rollout and selective reflection ( Pan et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ) . EMAS uses recurring execution diagnoses to propose prompt and topology revisions, accepting updates through paired validation against the current system ( Fei et al., 2026 ) . MASFly and MANTA combine prior experience with execution feedback to support task-specific collaboration structures and execution-time reconfiguration ( Liu et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 经验驱动的方法研究执行知识如何支持后续协作，包括基于检索的智能体记忆、集体反思以及可复用的编排知识（Yang et al., 2025; Hao et al., 2026c; Lin et al., 2026）。 AgentNet 将基于检索的记忆与去中心化协调相结合，根据局部专长和上下文自适应地调整连接关系与任务路由。 DecentMem 为每个智能体提供独立的记忆池，分别存储已整合的经验和生成的探索性候选，并通过在线反馈调整二者的相对权重（Hao et al., 2026a）。 Meta-Team 保留个体执行上下文，并支持任务后的证据交换，从而促进智能体行为、智能体间协调以及团队组织的演化。 基于技能的方法将可复用知识与多智能体协作的变更联系起来：SkillMAS 将技能演化与证据引导的多智能体系统重构相耦合，而 Skill-MAS 将编排知识表示为可演化的元技能（Meta-Skill），并通过多轨迹 rollout 和选择性反思不断精炼（Pan et al., 2026; Lin et al., 2026）。 EMAS 利用周期性的执行诊断提出提示与拓扑修订建议，并通过与当前系统进行成对验证来接受更新（Fei et al., 2026）。 MASFly 和 MANTA 将先验经验与执行反馈相结合，以支持面向特定任务的协作结构以及执行时的重构（Liu et al., 2026; Huang et al., 2026）。

paragraphs.en: These studies demonstrate several ways to improve collaboration through structural optimization and experience reuse. ( Feng et al., 2026 ) Our work focuses on sustaining such improvement across heterogeneous task requirements, where coordination knowledge must remain appropriate to the team using it. EvoTeam maintains a library of reusable teams, selecting or creating teams according to collaboration requirements. paragraphs.en: A. Interaction rules provide soft coordination guidance about the information and evidence required at a handoff. They do not prescribe a complete execution sequence. The Chairman establishes task-specific assignments and can reassign subtasks when progress is blocked. For each handoff, the sending agent assesses rule applicability using the sender–recipient pair, the rule’s trigger, and the current information-transfer requirements. When a rule applies, the agent adapts its message to the current task while following the relevant information and verification requirements. If no rule applies, the agent communicates directly without imposing an unrelated rule (Section 3.2 ; Appendix D.4 ).
paragraphs.zh: A. 交互规则为交接点所需的信息与证据提供软性协调指导。 它们并不规定完整的执行顺序。 主席负责确定针对具体任务的任务分配，并在进展受阻时重新分配子任务。 对于每次交接，发送方智能体依据发送方—接收方组合、规则的触发条件以及当前的信息传递要求来评估规则的适用性。 当某条规则适用时，智能体在遵循相关信息与验证要求的同时，使其消息适应当前任务。 如果没有规则适用，智能体则直接进行沟通，而不强行套用不相关的规则（第3.2节；附录D.4）。

This separation allows compatible tasks to share and refine interaction rules without directly modifying other teams’ rule sets.
